_meta.indication: OFEV is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled; patients randomized 3:2 to OFEV 150 mg BID or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥40 years with IPF (ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT criteria) diagnosed <5 years, with FVC ≥50% of predicted and mild to moderate disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annual rate of decline in FVC
pivotal_trials.n: Nintedanib 150 mg BID n=309, placebo n=206
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted treatment difference in annual rate of FVC decline 125 mL/year (95% CI 78, 173); p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): diarrhea (62% vs 18% placebo), nausea (24% vs 7%), abdominal pain (15% vs 6%), vomiting (12% vs 3%), liver enzyme elevation (14% vs 3%), decreased appetite (11% vs 5%), weight decreased (10% vs 3%), headache (8% vs 5%), and hypertension (5% vs 4%).
target_moa: Nintedanib is a small molecule that inhibits multiple receptor tyrosine kinases including PDGFR α and β, FGFR 1-3, VEGFR 1-3, and FLT3.

rems.type: Sponsor stated that they did not plan to submit a REMS; no REMS was required for approval

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions requiring advisory committee input

summary.text: Nintedanib was developed as a 505(b)(1) NDA for IPF and granted orphan, fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations; the application received Priority review and was approved first cycle on the basis of three randomized, placebo-controlled trials (two pivotal confirmatory Phase 3 trials, 1199.32 and 1199.34, plus the Phase 2 dose-ranging Study 1199.30) showing reduction in annual FVC decline.

citations.quote: Nintedanib is a new molecular entity of the class of kinase inhibitor, and has been granted orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough designations.

Boehringer Ingelheim (BI) submitted the results of three 52-week, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, clinical trials in patients with IPF (Studies 1199.30, 1199.32 and 1199.34) to support the efficacy of nintedanib to treat IPF. Studies 1199.32 and 1199.34 were replicate, confirmatory, phase 3 studies of nintedanib 150 mg twice daily (BID) compared to placebo. Study 1199.30 was a phase 2 dose-ranging study of similar design. Although Study 1199.30 was designated as supportive data by the Applicant, due to the similar design/duration and inclusion of the treatment arm of interest, the nintedanib 150 mg BID and placebo treatment arms of Study 1199.30 were evaluated by this reviewer as pivotal study data to support the efficacy of nintedanib.
